identity.title: Structural and Functional Characterization of the N-Prenyltransferase DsKabA in Algal Neurotoxin Biosynthesis.

content.abstract: Kainic acid (KA) is a neuroactive natural product from the red alga Digenea simplex. Its biosynthesis begins with DsKabA, an N-prenyltransferase that converts l-glutamate and dimethylallyl pyrophosphate into prekainic acid, the first committed intermediate. Here, we combined LC-MS activity assays, X-ray crystallography, SAXS, molecular docking, ITC, MD simulations, and mutagenesis to characterize DsKabA. Product analysis confirmed prekainic acid formation, and kinetic measurements yielded apparent Km values of 1.03 +/- 0.16 muM for DMAPP and 52.25 +/- 1.61 mM for l-Glu. The 2.85 A apo structure revealed open and closed conformations involving the alpha7-loop-alpha8 region near the active site. Docking, ITC, and mutagenesis support Mg2+-dependent donor binding, ordered l-Glu association, and roles for Y403, H406, E407, M114, and M118 in catalysis and prenyl-donor recognition. These findings provide structural and mechanistic insight into the first committed step of KA biosynthesis.
